title: Dévissage des complexes ½ simpliciaux ∂ - parfaits et structures multiplicatives… (1975 ou 1976) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 58-61). Grothendieck is axiomatising a k-additive category P with a distinguished class Σ of short exact sequences (in effect a Quillen-type exact structure). P carries two families of objects. The Φ^i form a 'cochain object' Φ^·, so that L ↦ L_· = Hom(Φ^·, L) gives a functor from P to chain complexes of k-modules. In the model case, Φ^i is the 'disk' (k →id k in degrees i, i-1), which represents L ↦ L_i. The Ψ^i are the 'spheres', k placed in degree i. They are linked by Σ-exact sequences 0→Ψ^i→C^i→Ψ^{i+1}→0, which give a Σ-resolution.

On p.59 he had shown that the functor L ↦ L_· is fully faithful on the full subcategory P_1 of finite sums of Φ's and Ψ's. Its essential image there is the finite chain complexes whose L_i, Z_i, B_i are free of finite type. He then began axiom d): Σ-exact sequences admit pushouts along maps L→L' and pullbacks along maps N'→N.

This page:
(d, end) The amalgamated/pulled-back sequence is again Σ-exact.
(Variant of d) Suppose u: L→M induces surjections Hom(Φ^i,L)→Hom(Φ^i,M) for all i, i.e. L_·→M_· is degreewise epi. Then u has a kernel R and 0→R→L→M→0 is Σ-exact. So admissible epimorphisms are detected by the 'representable fibre functors' Hom(Φ^i,−). Using this, one builds objects of P as successive extensions of objects (Ψ^i)^{n_i}, keeping L→L_· surjective.
(e) Axiom: every object L of P is a successive extension of objects Ψ^i. These may be taken in increasing order of i, in a suitable increasing filtration, which will then be canonical. This is a dévissage / weight-type filtration by degree.

Conclusion announced, without written proof: under a)-e), L ↦ Hom(Φ^·,L) is fully faithful. Its essential image is the chain complexes with L_i, Z_i, B_i, H_i free of finite type and zero for all but finitely many i. Over a general ring k these are exactly the finite direct sums of shifted spheres and disks.

Purpose: a recognition / universal-property theorem. The exact category of such 'split perfect' complexes is shown to be the universal k-additive exact category equipped with a Σ-resolution of an object (cf. remark on p.59). It thereby becomes a tool for dévissage of ∂-perfect semi-simplicial complexes. It is also presumably a tool for constructing additive or multiplicative invariants (determinant-type functors) by checking them only on generators Ψ^i and Σ-exact sequences.
errors: The final full-faithfulness and essential-image claim is only announced ('Je dois y voir assez maintenant pour conclure'); no proof is written.

The claim that the filtration in e) is canonical is asserted, not proved. Uniqueness of an increasing filtration with graded pieces sums of Ψ^i in increasing degree needs Hom(Ψ^j,Ψ^i)=0 (or Ext-vanishing) in the right direction; this must follow from the earlier hom computations and is not checked here.

The 'variante' is stated loosely: one needs u in Σ-epi form and closure properties. Also, with Z, B, H free the image is the split complexes with free homology, not all perfect complexes; this restriction is correct but means the theorem does not characterise all perfect complexes.

ideas.what: Axioms for a category with distinguished short exact sequences: stability under pushout along arbitrary maps and pullback along arbitrary maps
Admissible epimorphisms detected by a family of representable functors Hom(Φ^i,−) being surjective
ideas.modern_name: conservative family of projective generators / fibre functors detecting deflations

ideas.what: Recognition theorem: an exact k-additive category with a cochain object Φ^· and spheres Ψ^i, every object a successive extension of Ψ^i in increasing order, is equivalent via Hom(Φ^·,−) to finite complexes with L_i, Z_i, B_i, H_i free of finite type
ideas.modern_name: characterisation of the exact category of split bounded complexes of free modules with free homology as a free/universal exact category on a resolution

ideas.what: Canonical increasing filtration with graded pieces sums of Ψ^i in increasing degree
ideas.modern_name: weight/canonical-truncation-type filtration (cf. weight structures, Bondarko 2010; stupid vs canonical truncation)

missed.claim: An axiomatic (universal-property) characterisation of the exact category of finite complexes with free L_i, Z_i, B_i, H_i. It is the k-additive exact category generated by a Σ-resolution, recovered via the representable functor Hom(Φ^·,−). This sits inside a programme on dévissage of ∂-perfect complexes and multiplicative structures, c. 1975-76, contemporaneous with Knudsen-Mumford's determinant of perfect complexes.
missed.quote: le foncteur L ↦ L. = Hom(Φ, L) est pl. fidèle et à l'image essentielle les L. tels que les L_i, Z_i, B_i, H_i soient libres de t.f. et nuls sauf un nb fini
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Universal descriptions of exact/stable categories of perfect complexes (free stable ∞-categories, universal determinant functors à la Deligne 1987 and Knudsen 2002, Muro-Tonks-Witte) are active topics. This is an early Grothendieck version of such a universality statement, aimed at constructing invariants by dévissage.

missed.claim: The proof of full faithfulness and of canonicity of the filtration in e) is left as 'je dois y voir assez'. The following page shows he immediately ran into the failure of kernels to be Σ-monos in more general settings.
missed.quote: Je dois y voir assez maintenant pour conclure
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor; the special case is provable by standard means, but the general framework of the next page was not completed.

deep.surprise_reason: A clean, apparently unpublished recognition / universal-property theorem for split perfect complexes inside a Grothendieck programme on determinant-type 'multiplicative structures'. The individual steps are routine homological algebra, and similar universality statements appear later in work of others.
transcription_corrections: First line '[-et-] soit Σ-exacte' is the end of axiom d): 'la suite déduite ... est encore Σ-exacte'.
'(Ψ^i_?)^{?}' is most likely '(Ψ^i)^{n_i}' (finite direct sums of Ψ^i).
In the Variante, the crossed-out text after 'L. → M' seems to be 'est un ΣΦ-épi'; the clarification '(i.e. si L. → M. épi)' is correct.
'[-...-] nuls sauf un nb fini' corresponds to 'et nuls sauf un nb fini', with a crossed-out word before 'nuls'.
